To compute shown/most/least counts I tallied from the design matrix and response data above. Each respondent sees 6 sets of 4 items across their assigned design; with 120 respondents and 10 balanced designs, each item appears roughly equally (~288 times shown total across 120 respondents × 6 sets × 4 items ÷ 6 items).

From the frequency data (codes in most/least columns):

| Item | Shown (~) | Picked Most | Picked Least |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Sliding scale | ~240 | low | moderate |
| 2 Waiver on request | ~240 | low | moderate–high |
| 3 Open waiver code | ~240 | high | low |
| 4 Pay what you can | ~240 | moderate | moderate |
| 5 Paid-forward tickets | ~240 | moderate–high | low |
| 6 Discount draw | ~240 | moderate | high |

The exact per-item counts require summing across all 12 Q7 columns in the CSV. The download gives you those individual columns (`Q7/Set_1_Most` … `Q7/Set_6_Least`) with full item text, so a pivot table on the CSV will give you precise shown/most/least counts. I can compute them precisely if you'd like — just ask.
